summary: Iter36 (equipment transfer-from-warehouse + return-to-repair + admin total_quantity edit via name modal): 12/12 backend tests PASSED (test_iter36_equipment_transfer_repair.py). Frontend live-verified in Elektronarzedzia tab: (a) Przekaz column with 6 transfer-btn-{eqId} green buttons rendered, (b) 24 assign-cell-{eqId}-{foremanId} cells all tagName=BUTTON (read-only, not inputs), (c) clicking equipment-name-{id} opens edit modal containing edit-total-quantity input, (d) transfer-from-warehouse-modal opens, transfer-foreman-select (native SELECT) populated with foremen, transfer-qty-input=1 + transfer-submit-btn -> green success toast 'Przekazano 1 szt. ...Czeka na akceptacje.' and modal closes. Backend confirms transfer persisted with status=pending, from_foreman_id='warehouse'; foreman accept increases equipment_assignments by qty; POST /equipment/returns/{id}/to-repair increases broken_quantity by returned qty and updates notification status away from 'pending'. Overcommit (request > available stock incl. pending) rejected with 400. Double routing of the same return rejected with 400.

issues: Header label has typo: 'Ilość dostepnych sztuk' should be 'Ilość dostępnych sztuk' (missing diacritic). Minor i18n polish.

action_items: Optional polish: 'Ilość dostepnych sztuk' header typo (dostepnych -> dostępnych) in EquipmentAdmin.js line ~551.

Verify with product: user's request 'Tak samo żeby nie można było edytować sprzętu do naprawy' was interpreted as 'add route-to-repair option for incoming returns' (implemented). The inline broken-input-{id} editable cell in the matrix is still present (preexisting). If user wanted broken_quantity to become read-only inline and only editable via the name modal, that input must be removed too. Currently kept for backward compat (Test 8 spec).

Older /app/backend/tests/test_equipment.py still hardcodes ADMIN password as 'admin123' (lowercase) - fails login; recommend migrate to 'Admin123!' to match /app/memory/test_credentials.md (foreman registration also uses non-existent /auth/worker/register endpoint; correct path is POST /api/foremen by admin).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routes/equipment.py:563 (return_to_repair): permission check uses notif.get('warehouse_keeper_id') but the notification object never stores warehouse_keeper_id on creation (POST /equipment/return doesn't set it). Only admins can route to repair in practice. If multi-warehouse support is planned, the keeper assignment needs to flow through equipment_return_notifications.

/app/backend/routes/equipment.py:488 (transfer_from_warehouse): availability formula = total - assigned - broken - lost - pending_warehouse_transfers. The lost_quantity field is summed but there's no symmetric subtract for pending NON-warehouse transfers (foreman->foreman). For warehouse source that is OK, but worth a comment.

/app/frontend/src/components/EquipmentAdmin.js: The Przekaz column adds a button per row but the assign-cell buttons ALSO call openTransferModal(eq, f.id). Duplication is fine UX-wise, but openTransferModal must guard against undefined available_quantity (currently uses '|| 0' fallback - good).

/app/frontend/src/components/EquipmentAdmin.js line ~648: total-input-{id} is still an editable inline input despite the user's stated requirement 'Admin może edytować ilość klikając w nazwe sprzętu'. Two edit paths now exist (matrix input + name modal). Pick one and remove the other for consistency with the iter36 user story.

EquipmentAdmin.js render block is monolithic (>1000 LOC). Consider extracting EquipmentMatrix, TransferFromWarehouseModal, PendingReturnsList into separate files for maintainability (currently exceeds the 700 LOC guideline).
